catalog_locator: single page, right column, section 'The Language' (file the copy we hold, text layer of(live HTML the copy we hold)
catalog_quote: Preliminary analysis of Khamba data (phonology and clause), as expected, shows that Khamba is attributed with typological features of Tibeto-Burman language spoken in Northeast India, for example, the clausal structure of Khamba has a SVO pattern and tonal features are noticed. A Tibetan script is used for literary work. Kagiu Boom, Yokar and Tengur are some of the books written in Khamba using a Tibetan Script. No linguistic research or documentation has done yet on this language.
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Quote: (1 p., PDF metadata khamba.cdr, CIIL, created 2016-06-01) text layer read with extracted text: right column reads exactly 'Preliminary analysis of Khamba data (phonology and clause), as expected, shows that Khamba is attributed with typological features of Tibeto-Burman language spoken in Northeast India, for example, the clausal structure of Khamba has a SVO pattern and tonal features are noticed.' followed (after two sentences on Tibetan script) by 'No linguistic research or documentation has done yet on this language.' The reader's ellipsis correctly spans the script sentences; wording is verbatim. Same text confirmed live today via direct download at sppel.org/resources/language-…
new_statements.rule_in_words: No rule for word stress is stated anywhere. The only first-hand prosodic remark on Khamba proper is CIIL-SPPEL's preliminary field observation that the language shows tonal features; stress/accent placement is not mentioned in any accessible source (the one accessible phonology page, Badu 2002 on the closely related Memba of Mechuka, lists segments only).
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is a preliminary project note, not a phonological analysis; no word/phrase domain given. Family-level context only (Tournadre & Suzuki 2023 sec. 7.3.3-7.3.4: in tonal Tibetic/Kham varieties pitch is primary and the first two syllables form a trochaic strong-weak unit) -- not specific to this language.
new_statements.identity_note: Target is Khamba [kbg] proper: c. 500-1,300 speakers in Nyering, Nyukong, Yortong, Mankota, Tasigong, Singha, Shimoling (Singa circle / Yang Sang Chu valley, Tuting subdivision, Upper Siang). The only accessible source with a 'Phonology' section, Badu 2002, describes MEMBA of Mechuka (West Siang/Shi-Yomi), a closely related Bodish variety with no ISO code of its own that Glottolog files under kham1283 ('Memba of the Mechuka valley =.. very similar to Khamba [kbg]'); Akanksha 2022 likewise describes Memba. Do not confuse with the Khamba of Manipuri literature (Khamba-Thoibi) or Khams Tibetan [khg] 'Khampa'.
